questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How stage magicians do their tricks in front of a crowd
Why so many people want to quit smoking but can't
Hypnotism and what makes some people easier to hypnotise
How to fall asleep more quickly after a stressful day
questions.why: They discuss hypnotism and why some people are more hypnotisable than others.

questions.q: What happens when Rob tries to hypnotise Sam at the start?
options: Sam falls asleep
Sam starts clucking like a chicken
Sam gets angry with Rob
It doesn't work
questions.why: Sam says, 'I don't think so, Rob. It's not so easy to put me into a hypnotic trance.'

questions.q: What real benefit of hypnotism does Sam mention?
options: Improving memory
Curing phobias
Making people more intelligent
Helping people learn languages
questions.why: Sam says hypnotism has real benefits, such as curing phobias.

questions.q: What is Rob's concern about hypnotism?
options: He doesn't want a stranger in his head
It is too expensive for most people
It only works on children
It takes too long
questions.why: Rob asks why you would let a complete stranger inside your head.

questions.q: According to Professor Amir Raz, which old ideas about hypnotism have been largely rejected?
options: That hypnotism is real and can be used in medicine
That relaxing helps people to become hypnotised
That clever people and men are harder to hypnotise
That hypnotists need a swinging watch to work
questions.why: He says the ideas about intelligent people and males being less suggestible have been largely dismissed.

questions.q: What does Professor Raz mean by 'absorption'?
options: Being able to get completely involved in an activity
Being able to remember a lot of information
Being easily influenced by others
Being able to relax your body
questions.why: He describes it as the ability to get engrossed, like losing track of time reading a book.

questions.q: Which example does Professor Raz give of absorption?
options: Playing a violin
Talking to a stranger
Doing a maths problem
Crying while watching a film
questions.why: He mentions people watching a film and beginning to cry, getting sucked into the scene.

questions.q: What is the second thing needed to be hypnotised, according to Professor Raz?
options: A soft and gentle voice from the hypnotist
Attention: focusing on certain things
A strong imagination and good memory
Being very tired or ready to sleep
questions.why: He says it's attention: the ability to focus and hone in on particular pieces of information.
